series.title: インターネットの歴史

ja: インターネットの前身ARPANETは、1969年にアメリカの4つの大学・研究所のコンピューターをつないで始まった。
easy: ARPANET, the start of the internet, began in 1969 by connecting four computers in the US.
std: ARPANET, the forerunner of the internet, began in 1969 by linking computers at four American universities and research institutes.

series.title: インターネットの歴史

ja: ネットワークを通じたメールで「@」を使ったのは、1971年のレイ・トムリンソンが最初。
easy: In 1971, Ray Tomlinson sent the first network email using the '@' sign.
std: Ray Tomlinson sent the first networked email in 1971 and chose the @ sign to separate user and computer names.

series.title: インターネットの歴史

ja: ワールド・ワイド・ウェブは、1989年にスイスのCERNでティム・バーナーズ＝リーが提案した。
easy: The World Wide Web was invented in 1989 by Tim Berners-Lee in Switzerland.
std: Tim Berners-Lee proposed the World Wide Web in 1989 while working at CERN in Switzerland.

series.title: インターネットの歴史

ja: 誰でも編集できる百科事典ウィキペディアは2001年に始まった。
easy: Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia anyone can edit, started in 2001.
std: Wikipedia, the free online encyclopedia that anyone can edit, was launched in 2001.

series.title: インターネットの歴史

ja: 世界の人口のおよそ3分の2がインターネットを使っている（2020年代前半の推計）。
easy: About two-thirds of people in the world use the internet.
std: Around two-thirds of the world's population uses the internet, according to estimates from the early 2020s.

ja: ナイル川の流域は、アフリカの11か国にまたがっている。
easy: The Nile River's area covers 11 countries in Africa.
std: The Nile's drainage basin spans eleven African countries.

ja: アマゾン川が海に流す水の量は世界最大で、世界の川から海に流れ込む水の約5分の1を占める。
easy: The Amazon carries more water than any other river. It is about one-fifth of all river water going into the sea.
std: The Amazon discharges more water than any other river—about a fifth of all river water entering the oceans.

ja: 長江（揚子江）はアジアで最も長い川で、全長約6300km。世界最大級の三峡ダムがある。
easy: The Yangtze is the longest river in Asia. It has one of the biggest dams in the world.
std: The Yangtze, about 6,300 kilometers long, is Asia's longest river and home to the Three Gorges Dam.

ja: ドナウ川は10か国を流れ、世界で最も多くの国を通る川とされる。
easy: The Danube River flows through 10 countries, more than any other river.
std: The Danube flows through ten countries, more than any other river in the world.

ja: 日本で最も長い川は信濃川で約367km。世界の大河と比べると短く、急な流れが多いのが日本の川の特徴。
easy: Japan's longest river is the Shinano, about 367 km. Japanese rivers are short and fast.
std: Japan's longest river, the Shinano, is about 367 kilometers long; Japanese rivers are typically short and steep.

ja: 知られている最古級の楽器は、約4万年前の鳥の骨やマンモスの牙で作られた笛。ドイツの洞窟で見つかった。
easy: Some of the oldest instruments are flutes made from bird bones about 40,000 years ago.
std: Some of the oldest known musical instruments are flutes made from bird bone and mammoth ivory about 40,000 years ago, found in caves in Germany.

ja: バイオリンは16世紀のイタリアで、今とほぼ同じ形になった。
easy: The violin got its modern shape in Italy in the 1500s.
std: The violin took on essentially its modern form in 16th-century Italy.

ja: ピアノは1700年ごろ、イタリアのクリストフォリが発明した。
easy: The piano was invented around 1700 by Cristofori in Italy.
std: The piano was invented around 1700 by Bartolomeo Cristofori in Florence.

ja: サクソフォンは、1840年代にベルギーのアドルフ・サックスが発明した。名前は発明者の名字から。
easy: The saxophone was invented in the 1840s by Adolphe Sax. It is named after him.
std: The saxophone was invented in the 1840s by the Belgian Adolphe Sax, who gave it his name.

ja: エレキギターは1930年代に登場した。大きな楽団の中でギターの音が聞こえるようにするのが目的だった。
easy: Electric guitars appeared in the 1930s so guitar players could be heard in big bands.
std: Electric guitars emerged in the 1930s, largely so guitarists could be heard over big bands.

ja: 虹は、太陽を背にしたときにしか見えない。空中の水滴が太陽の光を反射・屈折させて見える。
easy: You can only see a rainbow when the sun is behind you.
std: A rainbow appears only when the Sun is behind you, as sunlight is refracted and reflected by water droplets in front of you.

ja: オーロラは、太陽から来た電気を帯びた粒子が地球の大気とぶつかって光る現象。
easy: Auroras happen when tiny particles from the sun hit the air around Earth.
std: Auroras occur when charged particles from the Sun collide with gases in Earth's upper atmosphere and make them glow.

ja: 雪の結晶は基本的に六角形。水の分子が結びつくときの角度がもとになっている。
easy: Snowflakes usually have six sides because of how water molecules join.
std: Snowflakes are basically six-sided because of the way water molecules bond as ice forms.

ja: 夕焼けが赤いのは、太陽の光が空気の中を長く通るうちに青い光が散らされ、赤い光が残るから。
easy: Sunsets are red because the light travels through more air, and the blue light is lost.
std: Sunsets look red because sunlight passes through more atmosphere, scattering away the blue and leaving reds and oranges.

ja: 地球全体では、1秒間に約40〜50回の雷が落ちたり光ったりしている。
easy: Around the world, lightning flashes about 40 to 50 times every second.
std: Worldwide, lightning flashes roughly 40 to 50 times every second.

ja: 恐竜が地上に現れたのは約2億3000万年前の三畳紀。
easy: Dinosaurs first appeared about 230 million years ago.
std: The first dinosaurs appeared about 230 million years ago, in the Triassic period.

ja: ティラノサウルスとステゴサウルスの生きた時代は約8000万年も離れている。ティラノサウルスは私たちのほうが時代的に近い。
easy: Tyrannosaurus lived closer in time to us than to Stegosaurus.
std: Tyrannosaurus rex lived closer in time to humans than to Stegosaurus, which died out tens of millions of years before T. rex appeared.

ja: 約6600万年前、メキシコのユカタン半島付近に巨大な小惑星が衝突し、多くの恐竜が絶滅したと考えられている。
easy: About 66 million years ago, a huge asteroid hit Mexico. Most dinosaurs died out.
std: About 66 million years ago, a giant asteroid struck near Mexico's Yucatán Peninsula, a key cause of the extinction of most dinosaurs.

ja: 鳥は恐竜の子孫で、生物学的には「生き残った恐竜」と考えられている。
easy: Birds come from dinosaurs. Scientists say birds are living dinosaurs.
std: Birds descended from theropod dinosaurs and are considered by scientists to be living dinosaurs.

ja: 福井県は日本で最も多くの恐竜化石が見つかっている県で、新種も複数発見されている。
easy: Fukui Prefecture has the most dinosaur fossils in Japan.
std: Fukui Prefecture has yielded more dinosaur fossils than anywhere else in Japan, including several new species.

ja: 1957年、ソ連が世界初の人工衛星スプートニク1号を打ち上げた。
easy: In 1957, the Soviet Union sent the first satellite, Sputnik 1, into space.
std: In 1957 the Soviet Union launched Sputnik 1, the world's first artificial satellite.

ja: 1961年、ソ連のガガーリンが人類で初めて宇宙を飛んだ。飛行時間は約108分。
easy: In 1961, Yuri Gagarin became the first person in space. He flew for about 108 minutes.
std: In 1961 Yuri Gagarin became the first human in space, orbiting Earth in a flight lasting about 108 minutes.

ja: 1969年、アポロ11号のアームストロングとオルドリンが人類で初めて月面に降り立った。
easy: In 1969, Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin walked on the Moon.
std: In 1969 Apollo 11 astronauts Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin became the first people to walk on the Moon.

ja: 国際宇宙ステーション（ISS）には、2000年11月から途切れることなく人が滞在し続けている。
easy: People have lived on the International Space Station all the time since November 2000.
std: The International Space Station has been continuously occupied since November 2000.

ja: 日本の探査機「はやぶさ」は2010年、小惑星イトカワの微粒子を地球に持ち帰った。小惑星からのサンプル回収は世界初だった。
easy: In 2010, Japan's Hayabusa brought back dust from an asteroid. It was the first time in the world.
std: In 2010 Japan's Hayabusa probe returned particles from asteroid Itokawa, the first sample ever brought back from an asteroid.

ja: 人は人生の約3分の1を眠って過ごす。
easy: We spend about one-third of our lives sleeping.
std: Humans spend roughly a third of their lives asleep.

ja: 眠りには、目が素早く動く「レム睡眠」と、深い「ノンレム睡眠」があり、一晩に何度も繰り返す。
easy: There are two kinds of sleep: REM sleep and deep sleep. They repeat many times each night.
std: Sleep alternates between REM sleep, with rapid eye movements, and non-REM sleep in cycles throughout the night.

ja: はっきりした夢の多くはレム睡眠中に見る。
easy: Most clear dreams happen during REM sleep.
std: Most vivid dreams occur during REM sleep.

ja: 夜に明るい光、特に青っぽい光を浴びると、眠りを促すホルモンのメラトニンが出にくくなる。
easy: Bright light at night, especially blue light, makes it harder to feel sleepy.
std: Exposure to bright light at night, especially blue light, suppresses melatonin, the hormone that promotes sleep.

ja: 1964年、アメリカの高校生ランディ・ガードナーは、実験で約11日間（264時間）眠らずに過ごした。
easy: In 1964, a high school student stayed awake for about 11 days as an experiment.
std: In 1964, American high school student Randy Gardner stayed awake for 264 hours, about 11 days, in a sleep-deprivation experiment.

ja: 中世ヨーロッパでは、こしょうはとても高価で、お金の代わりに使われることもあった。
easy: In the Middle Ages in Europe, pepper was so expensive that people sometimes used it like money.
std: In medieval Europe, black pepper was so valuable that it was sometimes used in place of money.

ja: ナツメグとクローブは、かつてインドネシアのモルッカ諸島（香料諸島）でしか採れなかった。
easy: Nutmeg and cloves once grew only on a few islands in Indonesia.
std: Nutmeg and cloves once grew only in Indonesia's Maluku Islands, known as the Spice Islands.

ja: 1667年、オランダはナツメグの産地ラン島を手に入れる代わりに、イギリスにマンハッタン島（当時のニューアムステルダム）を正式に譲った。
easy: In 1667, the Dutch gave Manhattan to England and kept a small island where nutmeg grew.
std: Under the 1667 Treaty of Breda, the Dutch kept the nutmeg island of Run while England kept Manhattan, then New Amsterdam.

ja: サフランは世界で最も高価なスパイスの一つ。1kgを作るのに約15万個の花が必要とされる。
easy: Saffron is one of the most expensive spices. You need about 150,000 flowers for one kilogram.
std: Saffron is among the world's most expensive spices; roughly 150,000 flowers are needed to produce one kilogram.

ja: 唐辛子は南米が原産。16世紀にヨーロッパ人が世界に広め、インドや韓国の料理に欠かせないものになった。
easy: Chili peppers come from the Americas. They spread to Asia in the 1500s.
std: Chili peppers originated in the Americas and spread worldwide in the 16th century, becoming essential to Indian and Korean cooking.

ja: エベレストの標高は約8849m。2020年に中国とネパールが共同で発表した値。
easy: Mount Everest is about 8,849 meters tall.
std: Mount Everest stands about 8,849 meters high, a figure announced jointly by China and Nepal in 2020.

ja: エベレストに初めて登頂したのは、1953年のエドモンド・ヒラリーとテンジン・ノルゲイ。
easy: Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay were the first to climb Everest, in 1953.
std: Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay made the first confirmed ascent of Everest in 1953.

ja: 女性で初めてエベレストに登頂したのは、1975年の日本の田部井淳子。
easy: The first woman to climb Everest was Junko Tabei from Japan, in 1975.
std: Japanese climber Junko Tabei became the first woman to reach the summit of Everest, in 1975.

ja: ハワイのマウナケアは、海底のふもとから測ると約1万mあり、エベレストより高い。
easy: Mauna Kea in Hawaii is taller than Everest if you measure from the sea floor.
std: Measured from its base on the ocean floor, Hawaii's Mauna Kea is about 10,000 meters tall—taller than Everest.

ja: 富士山（3776m）は2013年に「信仰の対象と芸術の源泉」として世界文化遺産に登録された。
easy: Mount Fuji, 3,776 meters tall, became a World Heritage Site in 2013.
std: Mount Fuji, 3,776 meters high, was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2013 as a place of worship and source of artistic inspiration.
